# Pinned Hermes reader and callback inventory — Fix round 14

Source commit: `59004a62356f3a4697ab0fe8ad5086d2b405e2a6`. Scope: ALL 2100 original checkout Python files and ALL 1916 selected workspace Python files in `src/server/adapters/hermes/supported.json`; shared rows appear once. The test uses the selected disposable layout only and inspects no live installation or provider. Workspace additions are recorded below.

Counts: `{"delivery": {"bound": 76, "excluded": 246, "unreachable": 451}, "reader": {"bound": 27, "excluded": 104, "unreachable": 1290}}`. Bound includes explicitly replaced APIs and callers that necessarily pass through a checked binding. Unreachable means its delivery/read branch is not entered by the selected one-shot command under the generated config/environment; it is not a claim of Python sandboxing. Excluded are conservative grep/AST hits whose source is outside the requested config/external-callback semantics; they remain listed and checked so a new hit cannot disappear silently.

## Audit and evidence

Initial grep covered `open(`, `read_text`, `safe_load`, `load_dotenv`, `dotenv_values`, `config.yaml` and `.env` across the pinned source, including eval/build/skill scripts. `inventory.py` independently parses every pinned Python file, scans synchronous and asynchronous definitions and module-level code, records ALL supported file-read/parser candidates without function-local path keywords and config/env compatibility wrappers, callback invocations (including `context.run(callback)`, `cb(...)` and indirect injector calls), and every function in the core dispatch/ledger/loader/lifecycle/middleware/stream/shell/outbound modules. The test compares this complete supported-syntax candidate ledger and source hashes, never regenerates it, and appends constant-path/parameter readers and an async/method callback to the genuine cli_config_load.py in disposable scanner input. It rejects the original hash, then requires four unlisted additions with the updated hash; the mutated source is never imported or executed. Source edits or new definitions require a fresh audit and pin change; this is bounded static-source evidence, not dynamic whole-machine tracing.

- **B-SNAPSHOT:** `config.py` Snapshot.bind/bind_main. 25 identity slots after the real `cli` alias and `main` probe bind: user/raw/version/default/managed/env/secret/skills/CLI slots. An immutable captured value is the only source; callers receive fresh copies. CLI preserves pinned defaults, normalization, native merge, expansion, managed overlay and environment mirror. Dotenv mappings stay empty; both credential getters retain the explicitly selected process value. Real bindings exist before replacement. C swaps/restores YAML/dotenv after the successful check, checks backend/redaction/env/credential effects, defensive copies and every slot's identity. Production stop exits 125, so stock `except Exception` fallbacks cannot recover from refusal.
- **B-GUARD:** `guard.py` close_plugins checks the actual manager, empty callback containers/injection slots/event work and every replacement identity before delivery. It binds the existing `ainvoke_hook`, removes the nonexistent substitute, and checks `_delivery_manager` before execution middleware takes callbacks. G exercises real manager/public/lifecycle async delivery and middleware with callback-bearing state, zero callback/provider effects, clean empty results and identity substitutions. Startup sets `_discovered=True`; discovery returns [] and registration/task/ledger entries refuse.
- **U-TUI:** `main.py:281-299,1797` and `cli.py:1747-1781`: pipes and stream-JSON selection choose one query and return before the interactive process_loop. In particular `cli_info_mixin.py:824`'s direct YAML read at **858** is accounted for, not assumed snapshot-bound.
- **U-PARENT/U-REG/U-WORKER:** the named caller is replaced or cannot create registration/worker state; helpers are listed individually. The registry and guard remain a boundary for the trusted pinned runtime, not malicious arbitrary Python.
- **U-ENTRY/U-TOOLS/U-OPTION/U-ENV/U-SELECT:** the per-row evidence names the unselected command, rejected native tool, absent selector, fresh-shadow file or disabled branch. Source scripts are never executed by plain skill reads. The accepted Low write and network limits still apply.
- **X-DATA/X-CALL/X-HELPER:** reviewed false-positive candidates remain in the ledger. Runtime supervisor state/progress, native code identity, skill frontmatter and already supplied string parsing are not user/managed/dotenv config authority; private streaming/UI/provider callbacks are not external plugin delivery.

## Selected path additions in round 10

The context-engine lifecycle/selection family (`select_context`, `on_session_start`, `on_turn_complete`, `on_session_end`, `on_session_reset`, `on_session_switch`) and named selection/notification callers are explicit scanner candidates. U-CONTEXT means only the external-engine branch is unselected: the built-in compressor can receive those same calls. The frozen raw mapping has no context override; pinned defaults and `_select_context_engine` force `compressor` and return before plugin selection. The old compression-complete X-CALL exclusion was wrong and is replaced below.

Prefill is a startup call with an empty selector, not a missing call. Skin initialization runs at CLI import; only its file branch is absent because no skins are copied to the fresh run home. The context-length cache is intentionally run-owned **behavioral dynamic state**: it can change compression thresholds and is not included in frozen config. Bundled platform manifest reads populate environment-variable UI metadata, not plugin execution or environment values. All four have dedicated rows below.

Additional broad I/O candidates include writes, Image/webbrowser/openers, data parsers, native caches/locks and separate commands. Each stays in the checked ledger with its reviewed disposition; exclusions do not claim the containing function is unreachable. This finite AST scanner checks the supported spellings and pinned source, not arbitrary Python aliases, semantic equivalence or a whole-machine call graph.

## Workspace additions — Fix round 14

The selected editable finder imports the generation workspace. The validator retains the original 2,103 checkout pins and separately pins all 1,916 workspace Python files plus uv.lock, pyproject.toml and pm/lock.json (1,919 objects). The 240 newly pinned plugin files have the same bytes as the checkout. Their root __init__.py contains only a comment.
